name: TimeComponentServerFacet_SyncToClient
summary: The time facet's sync: head-only, the shared two-u64 BE head and nothing after it. 16-byte body, C2S. The card was absent from the atlas entirely; writer and reader both stop after the head and the committed 16-byte record reproduces byte for byte.
purpose: The time facet syncs the client's clock state to the server; the server changes its replicated time state. Head-only, so the server's only job is to parse the head and never desynchronize the stream.

created_when: the client syncs its clock with the server
lifecycle.if_absent: the server never receives the client's time sync

envelope: Record envelope (owned by javelin/frame.py, not a body field): typed header 00 01 followed by the prefix varint 98 42, i.e. type_dec 4248. A client channel-0 record carries that typed header at offset 24, after the 8-byte frame head and the 16-byte actor id.

fields.name: local_facet_id
fields.note: First u64 of the shared message head, and the sending facet's own local id - identity, not request data. The send builder fills msg+0x08 from FUN_1416c1c40(facet) = *[*[facet+8]+8] + [GDE+0x10]: [GDE+0x10] is the id handed out by the global id dispenser FUN_14144a9f0 at ClientGDE attach (writer FUN_141464890 <- FUN_14167c760), and *[*[facet+8]+8] is a base read off the object the GDE's server-GDE reference resolves to (FUN_1417db510). That same value is the key the facet registers itself under in the Context's facet map (FUN_14167c560: key FUN_1416c1c40(facet), value the facet object, slot array at Context+0x1b0) and the key the RMI dispatcher looks up, so it is the local id the server must address. The client names it itself: log field facetId, 'Failed to unregister the facet.', and on a duplicate collidingLocalId + collidingFacetName with 'We got a collision on facets IDs, RMIs may fail to be delivered to this facet.'; the dispatch failure line calls it targetLocalId. Measured 0x93a3e477cb5fd51e on the 2026-10-19 20:52 record; the same probe walk that named this facet found it among the four local ids registered for TimeComponentClientFacet in a different session, and the server's reply addressed to it dispatched 642 of 642.

fields.name: local_actor_id_word0
fields.note: Second u64 of the shared message head, and the first 8 bytes of the client's own actor id - identity, not request data. Writer FUN_1414dbca0 copies the message object's +0x10 through a stack local and writes it big-endian (htonl64 FUN_1461668a0) through the stream raw-write slot +0x40. The send builder fills +0x10 from FUN_1416be9f0, which dereferences the weak handle at the GDE's +0x60 (FUN_14165c230) and reads [session+0x88]. Measured 0xbf85314bbc4a951a in all 14 committed bodies of the six head-prefixed messages across five sessions; in the same records its little-endian bytes 1a954abc4b3185bf are the first 8 of the record's 16-byte actor id, the local player's actor id handed over by ClientAddEntryMsg (0xa4).

evidence.ref: Head provenance, recovered 2026-11-01: the shared writer FUN_1414dbca0 stores msg+0x08 (straight) then msg+0x10 (through a stack local) with FUN_140877280 = htonl64 FUN_1461668a0 + stream raw-write slot +0x40; the reader FUN_14150e670 mirrors it. This wire's builder FUN_14407b520 (sole caller FUN_14408d410) fills +0x08 with FUN_1416c1c40(...) and +0x10 with *FUN_1416be9f0(...) = [session+0x88]

re message-names 0x1098 -> record_fn 0x144086cf0 -> facet vtable 0x1482fff40 (slot +0x20 MARSHAL 0x1414c0730, slot +0x28 UNMARSHAL 0x144072d20) -> object vtable 0x1482ff7d0 (name accessor +0x08 -> 'TimeComponentServerFacet_SyncToClient' at +0x70); writer object vtable +0x60 = 0x14259f170 (jmp thunk to the shared head writer FUN_1414dbca0) / reader +0x68 = 0x14259f180. Both stop after the head.
